2608.03983.title: Can Large Language Models Recover Semantic Optimization Opportunities That Compilers Miss?
2608.03983.paper_summary: Optimizing compilers miss profitable transformations when their enabling semantics are absent from the analyzed program representation. We ask whether large language models (LLMs) can recover such semantics from heterogeneous C/C++ context and realize them as validated, contract-preserving artifacts. We introduce SeGaBench, an executable benchmark containing 100 synthetic and 20 source-backed cases spanning low-level assumptions, data-structure invariants, and high-level semantic lifting. Each case includes hidden enabling semantics, an oracle artifact, correctness and semantic validators, and a reproducible performance protocol. We evaluate five LLMs using five independent responses per case. The strongest model produces correct artifacts in 94.8% of responses, achieves at least 1.05x speedup in 83.3%, and obtains a performance success on 93.3% of cases. Nevertheless, correct artifacts often close only part of the oracle gap. These results show that LLMs can complement compiler analysis as speculative semantic proposers, provided that their artifacts are validated and evaluated.
2608.03983.paper_summary_zh: 優化編譯器在分析的程式表示中缺乏啟用語義時，會錯過有利的轉換。我們詢問大型語言模型（LLMs）是否能從異質的 C/C++ 上下文中恢復這些語義，並將其實現為經過驗證的、保持合約的工件。我們介紹 SeGaBench，一個可執行的基準測試，包含 100 個合成案例和 20 個源支持案例，涵蓋低階假設、資料結構不變式和高階語義提升。每個案例都包括隱藏的啟用語義、一個神諭工件、正確性和語義驗證器，以及一個可重現的性能協議。我們使用每個案例五個獨立的回應來評估五個 LLM。最強的模型在 94.8% 的回應中產生正確的工件，在 83.3% 的情況下實現至少 1.05 倍的加速，並在 93.3% 的案例中獲得性能成功。然而，正確的工件通常僅能縮小神諭差距的一部分。這些結果表明，LLMs 可以作為投機性語義提議者來補充編譯器分析，前提是它們的工件經過驗證和評估。
